stories.headline: An Uzbek trucker’s fatal Ohio crash exposed a web of ‘chameleon’ carriers
stories.summary: Fox News tied the July 5 death of 21-year-old UMass Lowell goalkeeper Tobias Forsythe on Interstate 71 to a wider pattern of trucking fraud in southwest Ohio. Authorities say Uzbek national Bekhzod Asrarov, 42, who entered on a diversity visa and held an Ohio commercial license, rear-ended Forsythe’s Honda and later needed Google Translate to speak with troopers. Court papers say he removed a dashboard camera after the crash. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said drivers who cannot read road signs should not be hauling 80,000-pound rigs. A local researcher told Fox that Uzbek-linked companies around Maineville have stacked up English-language and electronic-logging violations, the “chameleon carrier” pattern of firms that re-register after safety trouble.

stories.headline: Novak’s overtime winner saves the Penguins after they blow a four-goal lead to Montreal
stories.summary: Tommy Novak scored his second goal of the night 1:33 into overtime, a wrist shot from the right circle off Evgeni Malkin on a 2-on-1, and the Penguins beat Montreal 6-5 in the home opener at PPG Paints Arena. Pittsburgh had raced to a 5-1 lead before the Canadiens climbed back. Malkin finished with a goal and two assists, Erik Karlsson and Kris Letang each had two assists, and Arturs Silovs made 20 saves. Nick Suzuki had a goal and three assists and Cole Caufield scored twice for Montreal. Jakub Dobes stopped 24 shots. Novak said coming back with the two points after giving up a lead like that felt huge.

stories.headline: Watchdog asks NYC to probe Mamdani’s Signal chats with social-media influencers
stories.summary: A Texas watchdog has asked New York’s Conflicts of Interest Board to investigate Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s office over taxpayer-funded outreach to social-media influencers. Democracy Restored director Houston Keene wrote Friday that new-media aide Emilia Rowland set up an official Signal account and fed talking points to a curated list of more than 200 influencers, which he says breaks city ethics rules. The complaint cites an August Columbia Journalism Review report on the chat. Keene said the point of the channel was to move the mayor’s agenda, and that is what happened.

stories.headline: GOP bill would cut funds to states that treat raising a son as a boy as child abuse
stories.summary: Sen. Eric Schmitt and Rep. Mary Miller are pushing the Yaeli Martinez Child Protection Act, which would withhold federal money from states that take children from parents who refuse to treat them as the opposite sex or to approve medical transitions. The bill would also stop state courts from ignoring another state’s custody order when a child is taken across state lines for what the text calls sex-rejecting procedures. Sponsors point to the Texas-California standoff over Jeff Younger’s son and to Worcester, Massachusetts, voting to become a transgender sanctuary city. More than 30 groups are listed in support.

stories.headline: Brazil votes Sunday on whether Lula’s left loses another Latin American election
stories.summary: Brazil’s first-round presidential vote is Sunday, and Fox News framed it as the biggest test yet of Latin America’s turn away from the left after Colombia, Peru, and Chile. Datafolha has President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva at 42 percent and Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, at 38 percent, inside a two-point margin of error. Neither is expected to win outright. A runoff poll has Lula up by 3 points, but critics say Datafolha has a history of undercounting the vote against Lula and the Workers’ Party.

stories.headline: Japan protests after a U.S. Marine is arrested in a woman’s killing in Okinawa
stories.summary: Japanese officials said a U.S. Marine lance corporal was arrested Sunday on suspicion of murder and robbery after a woman’s body was found early Saturday in a Naha hotel. Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi confirmed the arrest, and Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said Japan lodged a strong protest with the United States over what she called a brutal and heinous incident. NHK identified the suspect as Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, stationed at Marine Corps Air Station Futenma, and the woman as 39-year-old Yagi Anna. U.S. officials did not confirm the name. The III Marine Expeditionary Force said it is cooperating with Japanese authorities and offered condolences.

stories.headline: Texas mother charged with capital murder after both sons are shot in Waxahachie
stories.summary: Ellis County deputies charged Colleen Nichole Lemmon, 42, with two counts of capital murder after a call just before 4:15 a.m. Thursday on Big Sky Drive in Waxahachie. Christopher Scott Pitre, 21, was dead at the scene. His 15-year-old brother died later at a hospital. An arrest affidavit obtained by FOX 4 says deputies found Lemmon with what appeared to be self-inflicted cuts on her wrists and a handgun nearby, and that she told officers, “I shot both my kids.” The boys’ father, Scott Pitre, told NBC 5 his younger son had just had a birthday and that he wants justice.

stories.headline: K-9 Otis leads Alhambra police to about 440 pounds of cocaine in an SUV
stories.summary: Alhambra police said K-9 Otis alerted on an SUV during a traffic stop on Valley Boulevard near the 710 Freeway, and officers found about 200 kilos, roughly 440 pounds, of cocaine packed in cardboard boxes. The driver, Julio Rangel of Huntington Park, first said the boxes were not his and that he was coming from a cousin’s house, then said he was taking diesel parts to a friend’s shop. Police booked him at the Alhambra station. The department said the load was more cardboard than an Amazon truck on Prime Day.

stories.headline: Southern Baptist president tells pastors to step into the midterms
stories.summary: Southern Baptist Convention president Willy Rice said pastors should engage the midterms because many political fights are moral and theological at the core. He argued that pastors have had a strong public voice at key moments in American history, and that the theological left has not hesitated to mix religion and politics. Rice said Christians have been pushed for decades, from outside and inside the church, to stay quiet and withdraw. He said that pressure should not keep evangelicals out of the campaign.

stories.headline: Kudlow and Moore: media skipped record incomes and a record-low poverty rate
stories.summary: Just the News argued that legacy coverage of the economy has left out figures economists Larry Kudlow and Stephen Moore highlighted in the New York Post. They said real median household income rose 2.6 percent to $87,460 in 2025, the highest inflation-adjusted reading since the series began in 1967, and that the poverty rate fell to 10.2 percent, the lowest on record. July jobless claims hit 187,000, the lowest since September 1969. Unemployment is 4.2 percent, about where it was in September 2024, even with gas near $4.50 a gallon. The two say Republicans can still win the affordability argument in November.

stories.headline: Judge says Trump administration cannot keep the boat-strike legal memo secret
stories.summary: U.S. District Judge Paul A. Engelmayer rejected the Trump administration’s bid to withhold a classified Justice Department memo used to justify lethal strikes on suspected drug boats. In a 66-page ruling he said officials cannot claim deliberative-process and attorney-client privilege after senior officials cited the Office of Legal Counsel opinion as the binding legal basis for the operations. The case grew out of FOIA suits, including one from the ACLU. The strikes have killed at least 200 people in international waters, OANN reported.

stories.headline: Canadian rock singer Sass Jordan dies at 65
stories.summary: Sass Jordan’s family said the singer, songwriter, Juno winner, and longtime Canadian Idol judge died peacefully on October 2, surrounded by family. She was 65. Born Sarah Jordan in Birmingham, England, she moved to Montreal as a child, was fronting club bands by 16, and spent four decades as one of Canadian rock’s best-known voices. Her publicist said she drew from Judas Priest, Ozzy Osbourne, and Anthrax as well as Al Green and Aretha Franklin. The family called her an irreplaceable force of nature.

stories.headline: Musk asks owners how they want their FSD, and fans pitch minivans and a 500-mile Cybertruck
stories.summary: Elon Musk asked Tesla followers on Saturday, “How would you like your FSD?” The post drew about 4.8 million views after he quote-posted a fan who wrote that people want Full Self-Driving and then go to tesla.com to pick the shape. Replies turned into a wish list: a seven-seat minivan, a three-row SUV, a 500-mile Cybertruck, and a new Model S Plaid+ with active aero. TeslaNorth said the question does not confirm a new vehicle or a customization program. It does show owners asking for body styles Tesla does not sell today.

stories.headline: Former FBI agent: investigators are quietly rebuilding the Lynette Hooker scene
stories.summary: Six months after Lynette Hooker, 55, vanished on an April 4 sailing trip in the Bahamas, former FBI agent Nicole Parker said the case is not closed. Her husband, Brian, told investigators she went overboard from a dinghy near Hope Town after drinks. He was questioned and released and has not been charged. The Coast Guard Investigative Service seized the couple’s sailboat Soulmate in May and sent divers in June. Parker, a former Crimes on the High Seas coordinator, said evidence went to the FBI lab at Quantico and agents are trying to reconstruct a possible crime scene on the water. Hooker’s mother has said she believes Lynette made it back to the boat.

stories.headline: Trumbull football falls 28–14 at Shelton; Eagles drop to 1–3
stories.summary: Trumbull High lost 28–14 to Shelton on Friday night and fell to 1–3, a second straight defeat. Cade Volpicelli still rushed for 43 yards and a touchdown and added 62 receiving yards. Shelton improved to 3–1. Trumbull’s next game is at Danbury at 7 p.m. on October 16. Shelton plays Sheehan on Friday. The town newsflash had nothing newer than items already in the archive.
